## Executed analysis complete — final hypothesis below

**HYPOTHESIS (submission text)**

Among Black NLSY79 respondents, having been jailed (`ever_jailed` = 1 during 1985–1994) is **associated with** markedly lower and, crucially, stagnant wealth, and the size of that wealth penalty depends on pre-incarceration economic position — though because no income variable exists in this NLSY extract, pre-incarceration wealth (`composite_wealth_1985` terciles) is used as a proxy for "income level" and is not a measured income construct. Restricting inference to Black males (`race` = "black", `sex` = "male"; n = 1,465, of whom 143 = 9.76% were ever jailed; Black females, 16 ever jailed at a 1.0% jail rate, are reported descriptively only and excluded from inference because the 9.8%-vs-1.0% rate difference is a confound, not extra power), `ever_jailed` is associated with `composite_wealth_1996` averaging $11,164 versus $55,544 for never-jailed Black men (gap −$44,380, bootstrap 95% CI −$57,131 to −$32,294; −$33,143 after 1/99 winsorizing; medians $0 vs $5,450; Mann–Whitney p = 9.4e-11). The association *widens* monotonically across the three waves on a scale-free, inflation-immune measure — jailed/non-jailed mean wealth of **0.575 (1985) → 0.538 (1990) → 0.201 (1996)** — and the process visible in the data is progressive failure to accumulate rather than a one-time level drop: from the mid-window year to the post-window year the jailed group's wealth is flat (winsorized +$578) while never-jailed Black men gained +$16,794 (difference in change −$16,143, CI −$25,499 to −$7,329). Only ~11% of the 1996 gap pre-existed in 1985 (−$4,853, CI −$8,342 to −$1,103), so ~89% accumulated during and after the jail window, and the level and change framings agree. Stratified by the income proxy, the dollar penalty rises steeply with baseline resources — T1 (1985 wealth ≤ $0; 63 jailed/518 not): −$19,408, ratio 0.276; T2 ($0–$5,000; 42/363): −$26,921, ratio 0.302; T3 (>$5,000; 38/441): −$86,395, ratio 0.164 — but this gradient is an *estimated* moderation only on the dollar scale (`ever_jailed` × T3 interaction = −$48,090, SE 9,754, p < 1e-6; joint tier × jail F = 12.70, p < 1e-5), whereas on the proportional scale the penalty is large and highly significant at *every* tier (IHS −1.15, SE 0.25, p = 4e-06) yet not tier-dependent (joint p = 0.489; rank-percentile model p = 0.346); the honest reading is that jail is associated with a roughly constant proportional wealth penalty of about four-to-five-fold at all baseline resource levels, which mechanically yields the largest absolute dollar loss among the higher-resource Black men. Direction and tier ordering survive 1/99 winsorizing, median-, rank- and IHS-based summaries, and dropping the five largest wealth observations; all statements are associations, not causal effects, since `ever_jailed` is self-selected (jail rate 12–16% in the lowest baseline-wealth deciles vs 6.8% in the top).

**Key figures (bullets)**
- Inferential sample: Black males n=1,465; `ever_jailed`=1 for 143 (9.76%).
- Mean `composite_wealth`: 1985 $6,564 vs $11,417 → 1990 $18,644 vs $34,646 → 1996 $11,164 vs $55,544 (jailed vs never-jailed).
- Ratio trajectory (inflation-robust): 0.575 → 0.538 → 0.201; 1996 ratio CI [0.110, 0.327] vs 1985 CI [0.342, 0.876].
- 1996 gap: raw −$44,380; winsorized −$33,143; median $0 vs $5,450; MWU p=9.4e-11; P(a jailed man's wealth exceeds a non-jailed man's) = 0.34 (1985: 0.46).
- Level-vs-change decomposition: −$44,380 = −$4,853 (baseline) + −$39,526 (change gap, CI −$52,559 to −$27,621).
- Tier gaps 1996: T1 −$19,408 / T2 −$26,921 / T3 −$86,395 (ratios 0.276 / 0.302 / 0.164). Tercile cutpoints = $0 and $5,000; 39.7% of Black men have 1985 wealth ≤ 0, so T1 is over-large by construction; <0/=/>0 robustness split gives jailed 7/56/80 and the same direction (−$33,965 / −$17,537 / −$59,926), so the gradient is not a 0-tie artifact.
- Interaction: dollar scale significant (p<1e-5), IHS/rank scale NOT significant (p=0.489 / 0.346).
- **Correction to my own preview:** the raw jailed *fall* from $18,644 (1990) to $11,164 (1996) is outlier-driven — bootstrap CI [−31.5k, +7.5k] spans zero, winsorizing flips it to +$578, Wilcoxon signed-rank p=0.67. I therefore claim *stagnation/failure to accumulate*, not a wealth decline.
- Black females (non-inferential, 16 jailed): means $1,662/$1,988/$3,494 vs $10,741/$24,731/$43,101; ratio ≈0.08 by 1996.
- Descriptive comparison (NOT causal DiD; treated cells 57/52/12/9): ratio 85→96 is 0.470→0.190 (white male), 0.256→0.542 (hispanic male) — the deficit is not Black-specific, but monotone deepening is.

**Three judgement calls you should see:** (1) I rejected the "wealth decline" language my own preview suggested because it did not survive winsorizing/bootstrapping; (2) I did not upgrade the tier gradient to a moderation effect, since it is significant only on the arithmetic dollar scale — a roughly constant *proportional* penalty mechanically produces larger dollar gaps up-tier; (3) the hispanic-male trajectory moves opposite to the black/white pattern, so I kept the comparison-group work strictly descriptive rather than leaning on it.

payload.workflow: 1) Inventory: confirmed 12,013 x 6 with zero missing values and NO income/education/occupation/AFQT/age/geography field, so 'income level' was operationalized as baseline composite_wealth_1985 terciles (documented as an approximation). 2) Sample restriction: inferential sample = Black males (n=1,465; 143 ever_jailed); Black females (16 jailed) descriptive only; no de-duplication, no external data, no geography design. 3) Skew handling: raw means, 1/99 winsorized means (pooled Black-male percentiles applied identically to both groups), medians/IQRs, and asinh(w/1000) IHS transforms, plus Mann-Whitney U tests and 5,000-draw bootstrap CIs. 4) Stratification: terciles (cutpoints $0 and $5,000) with treated/control counts reported alongside every stratified number, plus a <0/=/>0 split to test the zero-tie mass. 5) Pre/post framing: 1985 baseline / 1990 mid-window / 1996 post-window levels, 1985->1996 change, and the 1990->1996 segment, with the level gap decomposed into baseline gap + change gap. 6) Moderation: one pooled baseline-tier x ever_jailed interaction per scale (IHS levels, IHS change, winsorized dollars levels, winsorized dollars change, wealth rank percentile), baseline wealth controlled, HC1 robust SEs, joint F-test of the two interaction terms. 7) Inflation robustness: jailed/non-jailed wealth RATIOS per year (scale-free) as the basis of the widening claim. 8) Descriptive selection check across race x sex, explicitly not a causal DiD. Findings implemented in analysis/main_analysis.py, analysis/addendum.py, analysis/final_summary.py, consolidated in analysis/out/FINAL_REPORT.md with tables in analysis/out/*.csv.
